task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output:
User: Hello, yes... I'm having trouble with my phone. My mobile data isn't working properly — it either stops working completely or it's just so terribly slow. I'd really like to get it fixed, please.

A little about me — I'm John Smith, and my number is 555-123-2002. I'm not very good with all this technology, so I'll need you to be patient with me. I'm actually visiting France right now, and I don't have any Wi-Fi available, so my mobile data is all I've got.

turns.thought: I'd be happy to help you with that, John! Since you're in France, data roaming is likely the key here. Let me look up your account first.

I've found your account, John. Since you're in France, the first thing I'll check is international roaming on your line. Your line (555-123-2002) currently has roaming turned **off** — that's very likely why your data either doesn't work at all or crawls. Let me turn it on for you at no cost.

Great news — I've found your account, John, and I've already taken one important step.

Here's what I found:
- **Your line:** 555-123-2002 (Active, on the Premium Plan)
- **Your data usage:** 8.7 GB out of 15 GB this cycle (cycle ends Feb 28) — so you still have plenty of data left
- **International roaming:** it was turned **off** on your line, and since you're in France right now, that was the main cause of your problem. I've just turned it **ON** for you, at no cost. ✅

Now we need to make sure your phone itself is set up correctly. Could you do something for me?

**Look at the very top of your phone's screen** (the status bar) and tell me what symbols/icons you see there. I'm especially looking for:
- An airplane icon ✈️
- Signal bars (📶) — and how many
- Anything like "5G", "4G", "LTE", "3G" or "E"
- A Wi-Fi symbol

Take your time — just tell me whatever you can see, in your own words, and we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at that for you.

turns.thought:
Yes — you've put your finger right on it. That "poor / 1 bar" **and** the **2G** are exactly why everything feels so slow. The good news is that it has nothing to do with your plan: you still have 6.3 GB of data left out of your 15 GB allowance, so there's no shortage. Here's what's going on:

- **2G** is a very old, very slow type of connection — it was designed mostly for plain phone calls, not for today's internet. Your phone has gotten "stuck" on it. We want it on 4G or 5G.
- **VPN** — try not to worry. A VPN sends your internet through another company's server, and it can slow your connection down a great deal. It isn't dangerous, and quite often it gets switched on by an app without people realising. It's perfectly safe to turn it off.
- I've already switched **international roaming on** for your line from my side (that was off, and you need it while you're in France). Your phone also has a matching "Data Roaming" switch that we'll want on.

Could you do two small things for me? Take them one at a time, no rush.

**Step 1 — Turn the VPN off**
- If it's an **iPhone**: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → VPN → turn the Status switch off (or tap Disconnect).
- If it's an **Android** (Samsung, Pixel, etc.): Settings → Network & internet → VPN → tap the small gear/settings icon beside the connected VPN → Disconnect (or Forget).
- *Easier shortcut:* swipe down from the very top of your screen — you'll usually see a VPN or little key icon there — tap it to disconnect.

**Step 2 — Move off 2G onto 4G/5G**
- **iPhone**: Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Voice & Data → choose **5G Auto** (or **LTE** if 5G Auto isn't listed).
- **Android**: Settings → Network & internet → SIMs (or Mobile network) → Preferred network type → choose **5G preferred** or **4G/LTE**.

Nothing will be lost and nothing will be deleted — these are just connection settings.

When you've done those, could you look at the top of your screen again and tell me what it says now? I'm hoping to see more bars, a "4G", "LTE" or "5G" instead of 2G, and no more lock symbol. Take your time.
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh my, that's a lot of steps all at once. I'm afraid I can only manage one thing at a time — I get muddled very easily with these menus. Let me do the very first one you mentioned, the VPN thing, and then you can tell me the next bit after that.

Let me try to turn that VPN off now.

turns.thought:
You're doing really well — and you absolutely didn't do anything wrong. The VPN being off is genuine progress, so thank you for that. Please don't be discouraged: "stuck on 2G" is one of the most common and most fixable problems there is. We just haven't changed the right setting yet.

Here's the thing: from my side, your account looks completely healthy — your line is Active, roaming is now enabled on it, and you have 6.3 GB of data left of your 15 GB. So this is all about the settings *on the phone* itself, and there are still several things left to try. We'll work through them one by one.

**What I'd like you to do now — two checks:**

**1. Check your "network mode preference"** (this is the setting that decides which type of connection your phone is allowed to use — and it's the one most likely pinning you to 2G)
- **iPhone**: Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Voice & Data — tell me exactly what it's selected on (is it "5G Auto", "LTE", "3G", or "2G"?)
- **Android**: Settings → Network & internet → SIMs (or Mobile network) → **Preferred network type** — tell me what it's set to.
- If your phone shows a plain option called **"Check network mode preference"**, just tap that and read me the result.

**2. Check that "Data Roaming" is ON on the phone**
- **iPhone**: Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → **Data Roaming** — make sure it's green/on.
- **Android**: Settings → Network & internet → SIMs (or Mobile network) → **Roaming** → turn it on.
- *You can also just swipe all the way down from the top of your screen* and look for a tile labelled Roaming or a little globe/antenna icon.

Since you're in France, that roaming switch matters a lot. It's the phone's half of what I switched on for you on our end.

Once you've done those, tell me:
- what the network mode preference says, and
- whether the top of your screen now shows anything different (more bars, 4G/LTE/5G instead of 2G).

And a small tip that often helps a lot after changing these settings: **turn your phone fully off, wait about 30 seconds, then turn it back on.** That forces it to reconnect to the network fresh. If you'd like, you can do that right after the two checks.

Take all the time you need — I'm right here.
turns.execution_output: User: I'll do the first one — let me find that network mode setting and see what it says.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's exactly it! 🎯 "2g_only" means your phone has been told: *"you may only ever use the oldest, slowest connection available."* That's the whole reason your internet crawls or cuts out. Nothing is broken and you haven't done anything wrong — it's just one wrong setting.

And yes, please do change it. You **can't break anything** by changing this. It's completely reversible — if you didn't like the result, we'd simply set it back. So there's nothing to worry about.

**Here's what to pick:**
- If you see an option like **"4G/5G preferred"**, **"5G preferred"**, or **"4g_5g_preferred"** → pick that one.
- If you only see **"4G only"** / **"LTE"** / **"4g_only"** → pick that one instead. It's still enormously faster than 2G.

**How to actually do it:**
1. **On iPhone:** Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Voice & Data → tap **5G Auto** (or **LTE** if 5G Auto isn't there).
2. **On Android:** Settings → Network & internet → SIMs (or Mobile network) → **Preferred network type** → tap **5G preferred** or **4G/LTE**.

Just tap the one you want — it'll usually get a little blue tick or dot next to it. Then press Back or the Home button; it saves itself automatically, there's no "Save" button to hunt for.

**Then — and this bit really matters:** after changing it, please **turn your phone completely off, wait about 30 seconds, and turn it back on.** Changing this setting often doesn't take effect until the phone reconnects to the network fresh, and that's likely why earlier attempts didn't seem to help.

When it comes back on, glance at the top of your screen again and tell me what you see. I'm hoping for: more bars, and **4G, LTE or 5G** instead of 2G. If it still says 2G, don't worry at all — that just means we move on to the next fix, and I've got several left up my sleeve. You're doing great.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll trust you on this. Let me change it to the 4G/5G one.

turns.thought:
That's fantastic news, John — four bars, "Excellent", and **5G**! That's as good as it gets. You've gone from the very worst connection to the very best, and you did it yourself.

Let me just double-check a couple of things on our side before I answer your questions.

Very glad to hear it, John — that's wonderful news. 😊

**Four bars, "Excellent", and 5G** — that's the best result we could have hoped for, and a huge improvement on one bar of 2G. You've fixed it.

**About the restart — no, you don't need to.** That was only because changing the setting *sometimes* needs a reboot to take effect. Yours took effect immediately, so there's nothing to fix. Leave it as it is.

**And please, don't worry about your photos.** Turning a phone off and on is completely safe — it's like closing a book and opening it again. Nothing gets deleted; photos, contacts, messages, apps, everything stays exactly where it is. Your grandchildren are perfectly safe. But as I say, you don't need to do it today.

**Now, the roaming question — good instinct to ask, that still needs doing.**

Here's the way to think about it: roaming needs to be switched on in **two** places, and I've already done one of them:

1. ✅ **On your account (my side) — DONE.** I switched international roaming on for your line 555-123-2002 earlier. I've just double-checked and confirmed it: it's **on**, at no cost to you.
2. ⬜ **On your phone (your side) — still to do.**

Even so, could you turn it on your phone too, please? Since you're in France, the phone needs its own switch on as well:

- **iPhone:** Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → **Data Roaming** → turn it green/on.
- **Android:** Settings → Network & internet → SIMs (or Mobile network) → **Roaming** → turn on.
- **Shortcut:** swipe right down from the top of the screen and look for a tile called Roaming, or a small globe/antenna icon.

*(Your data is all still included in your normal 15 GB allowance — this doesn't add any charge to your plan, it just lets your phone connect to French networks.)*

Once that's on, could you do a quick test for me — open a webpage, or send a photo message to one of your grandchildren? Tell me how it goes, and if anything at all is still not right, we'll keep at it together.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check on that roaming setting before I change anything — I don't want to switch it the wrong way.

turns.thought:
Yes — please go ahead and turn it on. And it's a very sensible thing to double-check before you do, John. Let me be precise about what I can confirm:

- ✅ **Turning roaming on is completely free.** There's no charge for switching it on, and I've already done the account side for you at no cost.
- ✅ **It does not change your plan.** You stay on your Premium Plan at $65/month, with the same 15 GB of data. Nothing gets swapped or upgraded — I haven't touched your plan.
- ✅ **Your data still comes out of your normal allowance.** You've used 8.7 GB of your 15 GB, so you have about **6.3 GB left** before this billing cycle ends on **28 February**. Any data you use in France is just counted out of that same 15 GB, exactly as it would at home.

I should be straight with you about one thing though: the tools I have don't show me international roaming *usage* rates, so I can't quote you a figure for what any individual megabyte abroad might cost. What I can tell you for certain is that enabling the feature is free and changes nothing on your plan. If you'd like the exact international rates confirmed before you use much data, I can pass you to a colleague who has that information — just say the word and I'll arrange it.

**But for now, yes — turn it on:**

- **iPhone:** Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → **Data Roaming** → switch it on (green)
- **Android:** Settings → Network & internet → SIMs (or Mobile network) → **Roaming** → on
- **Shortcut:** swipe down from the very top of your screen and look for a Roaming tile or a small globe icon

Nothing will be deleted and nothing else will change. Once it's on, do a quick test — open a webpage or send a photo message to one of your grandchildren — and tell me how it goes. If it's all working, you're sorted. If not, we'll keep going together.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll turn it on then.

turns.thought:
You're quite right to want to check properly rather than take my word for it — that's very sensible.

Let me be honest with you: I don't have a speed-testing tool on my side of the system, so I can't measure your connection directly. That means the most reliable test is a real one, done on your phone. Here's the simplest way:

**The test — pick whichever is easiest:**
1. **Open a webpage.** Open your internet browser (Chrome, Safari, or whatever you use) and go to a news site or any page you like. See how long it takes to appear and whether the pictures load.
2. **Or send a photo message** to one of your grandchildren — say hello from France! That tests your picture-messaging at the same time, and it's a lovely bonus if it works.

Either of those will tell you far more than a number on a screen would.

**Meanwhile, from my side, I've re-checked everything on your account and it's all as it should be:**

- ✅ Line 555-123-2002 — **Active** (no suspension, no billing problems)
- ✅ International roaming — **On** (confirmed just now)
- ✅ Data usage — **8.7 GB of 15 GB** used, so about **6.3 GB still available** until your cycle ends on **28 February**
- ✅ Your phone — four bars, "Excellent", **5G**, mobile data on, **Data Roaming on**, VPN off

So both causes of your problem are now fixed: the phone was pinned to old 2G, and roaming was switched off while you're in France.

Do give that page or photo message a try and tell me how it goes. If it loads quickly, you're all set and we're done. If it's still crawling, then I'd like to arrange for a colleague who has the full speed-testing and international-rate tools to take a proper look for you — just say so and I'll set that up.
turns.execution_output: User: Actually, hold on — I think I might have something on my phone that can check the speed. Let me try that, it seems more reliable than just guessing from a webpage.
